method: Independent lens review of captured evidence. The director opened every screenshot for a surface before scoring it, read the axe and capture results, and scored without sight of any other director's scores.
overallNote: Through the product-system-and-brand lens this baseline is a coherent app and a coherent marketing site that are only loosely the same company. The genuine tie is narrow but real and measurable: the accent is pixel-identical at #4f46e5 across Timeline's Share button, Tasks' Mark done, the landing hero's "outside", the about rail dot and the pricing eyebrow, and the grotesque is visibly one family throughout. Everything else diverges. The primary-button fill differs by property (marketing #111111, product #4f46e5, and a third light #f4f4f5 treatment on the app's dark chrome), the wordmark logic differs (baseline full stop in a near-invisible pale indigo versus a solid indigo-500 superscript dot), the app chrome never states the company name at all, and the eyebrow/label slot has at least four treatments across the seven surfaces. Inside the app, measured token drift is concrete rather than theoretical: the done green samples #1B873F and the overdue red #B13636 against documented tokens of #10b981 and #ef4444, and Notes puts the brand accent on a workflow state ("To review") in direct contradiction of the rule written into tokens.css. The clearest cross-view failure is Tasks board versus list describing the same task with different owners and different date formats. Two evidence caveats I will not paper over: the axe run reports zero violations across all sixteen captures, which is too clean to treat as meaningful assurance of the component layer; and every app capture carries the "In development. You're seeing it early." toast pinned bottom-centre, occluding content in the list view and Timeline, so some layout judgements are made around an obstruction. No surface reaches the 9.5 floor and none warrants a veto — nothing here is broken enough to embarrass the company, but nothing here yet reads as one design system either.

surfaces.rationale: Board and List share a real status vocabulary (To do / In progress / Review / Waiting / Done), the same dot+label+count header, the same Filter/Sort/Display toolbar, and a written empty state ("Nothing held up"). But the two views disagree about the same rows. The board card for T-1 shows a tag chip "Mara & Finn" and no owner; the list row for the identical task shows an "OR Orla" avatar chip in an Owner column — a user reads two different people for one task. Dates render in four formats across the pair: "Milestone due 1 Aug" and "Due today" and "Overdue by 2 days" on the board, "Milestone · 1 Aug", "Due 16 Jul", "Due 14 Jul", "Unscheduled" in the list, with "Order tonic" reading "Overdue by 2 days" on one and "Due 14 Jul" on the other. Token drift is measurable: the done mark samples #1B873F and the overdue red samples #B13636, neither of which is the documented --status-done (#10b981) or --status-blocked (#ef4444); only the amber in-progress dot hits its token (#f59e0b) exactly. The desktop list table is hard-clipped at the viewport edge — the Priority header renders as "P" and its values as "Hig", "Lo", "No" with glyph pixels running to x=1439 and no scroll affordance in frame. Mobile clips the column-pill row after "Waiting" with no fade, so Done is not discoverable there.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Make Board and List render the same fields from one component contract — one owner chip, one date formatter, one priority token — so a task cannot describe itself two ways; then fix the list table's right-edge clipping.

surfaces.rationale: The strongest system work in the app. The desktop detail sheet holds one grammar: breadcrumb, title, an inline chip row (To do / OR Orla / No due date / High), and a right meta rail where every section wears the same small-caps label (DESCRIPTION, RESOURCES, REPEATS, TAGS, CONTACT, PROJECT, SOURCE, COPIES). Exactly one earned accent moment — Mark done samples #4f46e5, dead-on the token — which is the discipline the token file asks for. Two component drifts: "DRAFT A REPLY" is set in small-caps, the identical treatment used for section labels, so a button is wearing the label style while every sibling button (Mark done, Add subtask, Attach, Make copies) is sentence case; and the keyboard hint card exists only on desktop. Mobile reorders rather than reflows — the meta rail (Repeats, Tags, Contact) lands below the comment composer, so the information hierarchy inverts between viewports, and a stray dark fragment of the app chrome peeks above the breadcrumb at the sheet's top edge.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Demote "DRAFT A REPLY" to the standard sentence-case button so small-caps stays reserved for section labels, and keep the meta rail above the composer on mobile to preserve the desktop hierarchy.

surfaces.rationale: The composer (Type / Voice / Photo segmented control plus Save note) and the two-pane notebook read as the same family as Tasks, and the note detail footer (Captured / Edited / In Tasks with a live task link) is a genuine cross-product tie. The systemic problem is colour semantics: the "To review" pill samples #4f46e5 — the brand accent — used as a workflow state, in the same viewport as the accent-tinted selected row (#eef2ff) and the indigo wordmark dot. The token file explicitly keeps the accent unambiguous between brand and to-do, and this surface breaks that rule; the sibling "In Tasks" pill uses a green (#166F34) that is again not --status-done. The inline row actions are three button variants in one group — Keep and Turn into task as outline buttons, Delete as bare red text with the smallest hit area for the destructive action — and they appear only on "To review" rows, so list rows have two different heights. Mobile strips the count badges off the Notebook/Review/In Tasks tabs that desktop shows (14/8/6), and the active Notebook pill is flush to the viewport's left edge, breaking the page's own gutter. "Save note" also becomes a full-width secondary, leaving the mobile composer with no visually primary action.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Move "To review" off the brand accent onto a neutral or amber status token so indigo means one thing per view, and unify the Keep/Turn into task/Delete row into one button group with a consistent destructive treatment.

surfaces.rationale: The best product-to-marketing tie in the whole set: the next-milestone node and the Share button both sample #4f46e5, pixel-identical to the accent on the marketing landing and about pages, and the display type on "Mara & Finn" is visibly the same grotesque as the marketing headline. The share state line ("Live since 15 Jul 2026. Anyone holding the link can read it.") is written, not defaulted. Against that: the control run in the header puts a segmented group (Timeline | Milestones) beside two standalone buttons (Preview, Share) at the same height, and the inactive segment renders as a filled grey button nearly identical to a secondary button — three button-ish shapes in one 350px run with an ambiguous group boundary. The breadcrumb is inconsistent with itself: "The Orchard, events" is plain text while the sibling "Mara & Finn" is a bordered select. On mobile the control row's Share button runs to the viewport edge while the content below sits on a gutter, and the signature axis is replaced by a vertical rail — a second independent implementation of the product's defining visual whose node and label scale does not match the horizontal one. Motion on the axis is not something these static captures can show, so I have given it no credit.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Resolve the header control run into one clear hierarchy — one segmented group, one secondary, one primary — and give the breadcrumb a single treatment instead of text-plus-select.

surfaces.rationale: The typographic voice is confident and unmistakably the same family the app uses, and the accent is exact: "outside" samples #4f46e5, matching Timeline's Share button and Tasks' Mark done to the pixel. That is the tie holding the two properties together — and it is doing nearly all the work alone. The primary CTA "See the system at work" samples #111111 black, while every primary action inside the product is indigo; the single most important button on each property is a different colour, which is the clearest two-systems signal in this baseline. The wordmark compounds it: marketing's full stop renders as a ~4px near-invisible pale indigo, whereas the app's mark is a solid indigo-500 (#6366f1) dot raised to cap height — related marks, not the same mark, and the app chrome never says "signal studio" anywhere, so a signed-in user sees no parent brand at all. Two competing label systems also share the fold: the mono uppercase eyebrow "NOTES → TASKS → TIMELINE" versus the app's small-caps sans labels for the same job. At 1440 the hero leaves a large empty right column and roughly 200px of dead space below the CTAs; mobile is the better-balanced composition.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Decide one primary-button colour for the company and apply it on both properties — indigo on the marketing CTA is the cheaper, truer fix — and align the wordmark's accent dot in weight and hue with the app's.

surfaces.rationale: The strongest single piece of writing and setting in the marketing evidence, and the indigo dot anchoring the left hairline rail samples exactly #4f46e5, consistent with landing and pricing. The eyebrow slot, though, is the third different treatment across three marketing pages: bold small-caps ink here, mono uppercase on landing, mono uppercase indigo on pricing — one slot, three type styles, two colours. The rail hairline itself samples a pale indigo (194,192,243) where the rest of the system uses ink hairlines, another one-off. Desktop composition is the weak point: the headline sets from x=122 while the body column begins at x=732 and starts below the headline's last baseline, leaving a very large empty rectangle under the headline that reads unfinished rather than composed; the single-column mobile version is materially better. The mobile capture also shows an open-circle-on-a-vertical-rule motif that is adjacent to but not the same as Timeline's mobile rail — two similar rail devices across the two properties that should be one.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Standardise the eyebrow to one type style and one colour rule across landing, about and pricing, then close the empty rectangle under the desktop headline by pulling the body column up onto the same baseline grid.

surfaces.rationale: I can only score what the capture shows, and the load-bearing component — the plan cards and actual prices — is below the fold in both viewports, so the thing my lens most needs to check for consistency with the product's chips, badges and buttons is absent. I have given it no optimistic credit. What is visible has real grid problems: the three-cell fact band is full-bleed while every other element sits on the ~160px content margin, and its dividers fall at x=533 and x=907, making cells of 533/374/533px. The first cell's text insets 160px to meet the page margin; the other two inset 28px from their own dividers, so the three facts align to nothing shared. On mobile the same band becomes three stacked hairline rows — a different component, and the "three facts side by side" reading is lost entirely. Copy compounds the incoherence: "Four ways in" promises four tiers, three facts appear, and the subhead names "Ethan" and the tiers "Pro" and "Enterprise" with no introduction and no counterpart anywhere else in the evidence. The eyebrow is accent-coloured mono here against about's ink small-caps.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Put the fact band on the same content grid as the rest of the page with three equal cells sharing one inset, and capture the plan cards so the pricing component can actually be reviewed against the product's own card and button system.
